I’m a doctoral researcher in Electrical Engineering at Chalmers University of Technology, where I am part of the Communication, Antennas and Optical Networks (CAOS) Division. My research focuses on trustworthy autonomous networks, with particular emphasis on uncertainty-aware learning and reliable decision-making for communication systems.

Current focus. I develop methods for uncertainty quantification, conformal prediction, and risk control in autonomous networks and O-RAN. My work studies how calibrated uncertainty can support dependable decisions under distribution shift, including optical quality-of-transmission estimation and multi-step channel state information prediction.

Background. I received my M.Sc. in Telecommunication Engineering, specializing in Signals and Data Analysis, from Politecnico di Milano. At STMicroelectronics, I developed quantization-aware, memory-efficient neural networks for continuous MEMS sensor self-calibration on resource-constrained hardware. Before joining Chalmers, I also worked across AI research, data science, and machine learning engineering roles at AGap2/RINA, DataLobster, Envision, and the PoliMi Data Science Association, with projects spanning industrial generative AI, anomaly detection, computer vision, and Edge AI.

Teaching & Supervision

I am a teaching assistant for Applied Object-Oriented Programming (EEN060/EEN065) at Chalmers, where I design examinations and lead Python exercise and laboratory sessions. In 2026, I supervised the completed bachelor’s thesis Autonomous Knowledge Agent: From Query to Report without Human Guidance.
